credentials.description: API key from the Wave Business portal (sent as Authorization: Bearer); it is tied to a real wallet — Wave documents no sandbox

example_prompt: Add Wave checkout to my e-commerce payment flow.

amount.description: Amount to collect, as a string. 0 to 2 decimals depending on the currency. XOF does not accept decimals. e.g. "5000" or "1500.50".

error_url.description: HTTPS URL Wave redirects the user to if the payment fails or is cancelled.

success_url.description: HTTPS URL Wave redirects the user to after a successful payment.

client_reference.description: Internal reference (max 255 chars) to correlate the session with your system. Returned in the response and in webhooks.

restrict_payer_mobile.description: E.164 number (e.g. "+221700000000"). If present, only this Wave account can pay this session.

aggregated_merchant_id.description: Aggregated merchant ID. Only for platforms that have enabled the Aggregated Merchants API.

id.description: Unique session identifier (prefix "cos-", max 20 chars). Store it before redirecting — required for verify_payment.

wave_launch_url.description: URL to open in the browser to launch the Wave payment. Do not open it in a WebView.

checkout_status.description: Checkout session state. 'failed' can appear in the context of the checkout.session.payment_failed webhook event.

business_name.description: Business name shown to the payer.

transaction_id.description: Wave transaction identifier (visible in the user's app). Absent if the payment is not completed yet.

when_expires.description: ISO 8601 UTC expiration timestamp. Default: 30 minutes after creation.

when_completed.description: ISO 8601 UTC completion or expiration timestamp. Absent if the session is still open.

success_url.description: Redirect URL after a successful payment, as provided at creation.

error_url.description: Redirect URL on failure, as provided at creation.

restrict_payer_mobile.description: Restriction E.164 number, if provided at creation.

aggregated_merchant_id.description: Aggregated merchant ID used for this session.

last_payment_error.description: Last payment error. Present only if payment_status is processing or cancelled.

code.description: Error code. e.g. request-validation-error, unauthorized-wallet, service-unavailable.

details.description: Validation details returned on request-validation-error. Each entry contains loc (field location), msg (message), type (error type). Can be null or absent (measured on 2026-10-24 on 401 errors) — check before iterating.

gotchas: Store session.id immediately before redirecting the user — it is the only identifier for calling verify_payment server-side.
wave_launch_url must be opened directly in the user's browser. Never open it in a WebView or an iframe — the payment will not initiate correctly.
By default the session expires 30 minutes after creation. After expiration, checkout_status changes to 'expired' and payment is not possible.
amount is a string, not a number. XOF accepts no decimals — send "5000", not "5000.00" or 5000.
The API key is tied to a single Wave wallet. To operate in several countries, get one key per wallet.
The Wave documentation describes no sandbox environment or test host: the only documented host is https://api.wave.com, and the API key is tied to a real wallet.

If the API key was created with request signing (optional Business Portal setting), every call must carry Wave-Signature: t={timestamp},v1={HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + raw body)} computed with the signing secret (format wave_sn_AKS_…, shown only once) — empty body for a GET. Without it: 401 missing-signature; other codes: invalid-signature, invalid-signature-format, invalid-signature-timestamp, expired-signature-timestamp (timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past or more than 30 seconds in the future). The setting is permanent for a key: to drop it, revoke the key and create another one.

[MUST TELL USER] The API IP whitelist turns on as soon as the first address is added in the Business Portal (Developer section) and can no longer be turned off from the portal — you have to go through your Wave account manager. Calls from an unlisted IP get 403 ip-not-allowed: on hosting without a fixed outbound IP (serverless functions, most PaaS), do not add any IP before you have a fixed egress.

Wave checks the key before anything else, even before routing: an invalid key returns 401 on any path. The no-matching-api-key message quotes the last 4 characters of the received key ("No API key found ending in '…'") — compare them with your key to spot a badly loaded environment variable. (Measured without a valid key on 2026-10-24.)
